nguy-n-dynasty.name: Nguyễn dynasty
nguy-n-dynasty.summary: The last Vietnamese dynasty, ruling unified Vietnam from 1802 until the French protectorate began in 1883, and nominally until 1945 when the last emperor abolished the treaty with France.

hawker-centre.name: Hawker centre
hawker-centre.summary: An open-air complex found in Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Indonesia, housing many stalls selling affordable meals as a more sanitary alternative to mobile food carts.

french-indochina.name: French Indochina
french-indochina.summary: A federation of French-ruled territories in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, that existed from 1887 to 1954, with capitals at Hanoi and Saigon.

fall-of-saigon.name: Fall of Saigon
fall-of-saigon.summary: The capture of South Vietnam's capital by North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975, ending the Vietnam War and leading to the country's formal reunification in 1976.

intangible-cultural-heritage.name: Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity
intangible-cultural-heritage.summary: A UNESCO designation, formalized by a 2003 convention, covering non-physical cultural heritage such as customs, traditions, language and craftsmanship.

prak-sokhonn.name: Prak Sokhonn
prak-sokhonn.summary: Cambodian politician, diplomat and journalist who has served as deputy prime minister and foreign minister since 2024, having previously held the same posts from 2016 to 2023.

prahok.name: Prahok
prahok.summary: A salted, fermented fish paste, usually made from mudfish, used as a seasoning and condiment in Cambodian cuisine, originally developed to preserve fish when fresh fish was scarce.

teochew-people.name: Teochew
teochew-people.summary: A Han Chinese sub-ethnic group from the Chaoshan region who speak the Teochew language; most now live outside China, especially in Southeast Asia.

hakka-people.name: Hakka people
hakka-people.summary: A Han Chinese sub-ethnic group whose ancestral homes are spread across southern China's border regions, historically late arrivals from central China who settled remote, marginal lands.

i-m-i.name: Đổi Mới
i-m-i.summary: Vietnam's economic reform program, launched by the Communist Party in December 1986, that shifted the country from a command economy toward a 'socialist-oriented market economy' while leaving political control unchanged.

khmer-rouge.name: Khmer Rouge
khmer-rouge.summary: The Communist Party of Kampuchea, which ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979 under Pol Pot as the repressive, totalitarian Democratic Kampuchea, responsible for mass deaths through social engineering policies.

vietnam-national-museum-of-fine-arts.name: Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts
vietnam-national-museum-of-fine-arts.summary: Vietnam's main art museum, located in Hanoi and displaying the country's fine arts across historical periods.
vietnam-national-museum-of-fine-arts.source_title: Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts

nanyang-style.name: Nanyang style
nanyang-style.summary: A mid-20th-century painting movement by migrant Chinese artists in Singapore, blending Chinese ink traditions with Western watercolor and oil to depict Southeast Asian subjects.

c-i-l-ng.name: Cải lương
c-i-l-ng.summary: A form of modern Vietnamese folk opera blending southern Vietnamese folk songs, classical music, Chinese-opera-based hát tuồng, and modern spoken drama.

tu-ng.name: Tuồng
tu-ng.summary: A classical form of Vietnamese theatre, often called Vietnamese opera, influenced by Chinese opera and distinct from the older hát chèo genre.

ch-o.name: Chèo
ch-o.summary: A form of satirical, often musical theatre traditionally performed outdoors by peasants in northern Vietnam, dating to the 12th century and taking its present form by the 16th century.

n-ca-t-i-t.name: Đờn ca tài tử
n-ca-t-i-t.summary: A genre of chamber music from southern Vietnam, also called nhạc tài tử, whose instruments resemble the ca Huế style with added guitar, violin and steel guitar; its best-known melody, Vọng cổ, was composed in 1919.

august-revolution.name: August Revolution
august-revolution.summary: A Viet Minh–led uprising against Japanese occupation and the Empire of Vietnam from 16 to 30 August 1945, ending with Emperor Bao Dai's abdication.

majapahit.name: Majapahit
majapahit.summary: Javanese Hindu-Buddhist empire based on Java that at its 14th-century peak held sway over much of Southeast Asia, before collapsing in 1527.

ubud.name: Ubud
ubud.summary: A town in Bali, Indonesia, promoted as an arts and culture centre, now a major tourist destination surrounded by farms and rice paddies.

5th-passage.name: 5th Passage
5th-passage.summary: An artist-run contemporary art space in Singapore active from 1991 to 1994, known for staging performance art and for a 1994 work that led to a decade-long ban on the art form.

nguy-n-cung.name: Nguyễn Đỗ Cung
nguy-n-cung.summary: Vietnamese artist (1912–1977) who helped make early portraits of Ho Chi Minh in 1946, chose the site for the Vietnam Museum of Fine Arts in 1963, and won the Ho Chi Minh Prize in 1996.

manila-metropolitan-theater.name: Manila Metropolitan Theater
manila-metropolitan-theater.summary: A historic Art Deco theater in Manila designed by Juan M. Arellano, opened in 1931, damaged in World War II, and later restored and reopened in 2021.

international-rice-research-institute.name: International Rice Research Institute
international-rice-research-institute.summary: An international agricultural research organization headquartered in the Philippines, founded in 1960, known for developing rice varieties that helped drive the 1960s Green Revolution.

bonifacio-monument.name: Bonifacio Monument
bonifacio-monument.summary: A 13.7-meter memorial in Caloocan, Philippines, designed by Guillermo Tolentino to honor revolutionary leader Andrés Bonifacio, founder of the Katipunan.

rizal-monument.name: Rizal Monument
rizal-monument.summary: A memorial in Manila's Rizal Park honoring executed nationalist José Rizal, with a bronze statue over his interred remains and near the exact site of his 1896 execution.

university-of-santo-tomas-main-building.name: University of Santo Tomas Main Building
university-of-santo-tomas-main-building.summary: The administrative center of the University of Santo Tomas in Manila, also housing several faculties and the Museum of Arts and Sciences.
university-of-santo-tomas-main-building.source_title: University of Santo Tomas Main Building

arthur-percival.name: Arthur Percival
arthur-percival.summary: A British Army officer (1887–1966) who commanded Commonwealth forces at the catastrophic defeat of the Battle of Singapore in the Second World War.

fall-of-singapore.name: Fall of Singapore
fall-of-singapore.summary: The Japanese capture of British-held Singapore in February 1942 during World War II, resulting in the largest surrender in British military history.

hms-repulse-1916.name: HMS Repulse
hms-repulse-1916.summary: A Royal Navy battlecruiser delivered in 1916, one of the fastest capital ships of her time, sunk alongside HMS Prince of Wales by Japanese aircraft off Malaya in December 1941.

hms-prince-of-wales-53.name: HMS Prince of Wales
hms-prince-of-wales-53.summary: A Royal Navy battleship completed in 1941 that damaged the German battleship Bismarck before being sunk by Japanese aircraft off Malaya on 10 December 1941.

paracel-islands.name: Paracel Islands
paracel-islands.summary: A disputed archipelago of small coral islands and reefs in the South China Sea, currently controlled by China but also claimed by Taiwan and Vietnam.

ho-chi-minh.name: Ho Chi Minh
ho-chi-minh.summary: Vietnamese communist revolutionary and statesman (1890-1969) who founded the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in 1945 and served as its first president until his death.

mao-zedong.name: Mao Zedong
mao-zedong.summary: Chinese communist revolutionary who founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and led it as Communist Party chairman until his death in 1976.

malayan-campaign.name: Malayan campaign
malayan-campaign.summary: 1941-1942 campaign in which Japanese forces, with air and naval supremacy, decisively defeated British Commonwealth defenders of Malaya at the opening of the Pacific War.

8th-division-australia.name: Australian 8th Division
8th-division-australia.summary: An Australian Army infantry division raised for overseas service in 1940 and destroyed as a fighting force by February 1942 in the fall of Singapore and nearby battles, with most survivors becoming prisoners of war.

ng-y-v-n-th.name: Ngụy Văn Thà
ng-y-v-n-th.summary: South Vietnamese naval officer (1943–1974), commanding officer of the corvette Nhật Tảo during the Battle of the Paracel Islands, killed when a Chinese missile hit the ship's bridge.

uss-serene.name: Nhật Tảo (USS Serene)
uss-serene.summary: A US Navy World War II minesweeper transferred to South Vietnam in 1964 and renamed RVNS Nhật Tảo, sunk in 1974 during the Battle of the Paracel Islands.

vietnamese-alphabet.name: Vietnamese alphabet
vietnamese-alphabet.summary: The Latin-based writing system for Vietnamese, devised in the early 17th century by Portuguese missionary Francisco de Pina and other Jesuits, using diacritics to mark 29 letters and tones.

classical-chinese.name: Literary Chinese
classical-chinese.summary: The written literary form of Chinese used from the 5th century BCE and adopted across Vietnam, Korea, Japan and the Ryukyus as a shared language of scholarship and administration until the early 20th century.

empire-of-vietnam.name: Empire of Vietnam
empire-of-vietnam.summary: Short-lived Japanese-sponsored state ruling Vietnam from March to August 1945 under the Nguyễn dynasty, proclaimed independent by Emperor Bảo Đại before Japan's surrender ended it.

ch-n-m.name: Chữ Nôm
ch-n-m.summary: A complex writing system adapting Chinese characters to write vernacular Vietnamese, used mainly between the 15th and 19th centuries by literati such as Nguyễn Du.

phan-b-i-ch-u.name: Phan Bội Châu
phan-b-i-ch-u.summary: A Vietnamese nationalist and revolutionary (1867–1940) who founded independence movements from Japan and China before being seized by French agents in 1925.

phan-ch-u-trinh.name: Phan Châu Trinh
phan-ch-u-trinh.summary: A Vietnamese nationalist and reformer (1872–1926) who sought to end French colonial rule through education and appeals to French democratic principles rather than violence.

tonkin-free-school.name: Tonkin Free School
tonkin-free-school.summary: A short-lived school founded in Hanoi in 1907 that offered free classes in modern subjects to reform Vietnamese society under French rule, shut down within months.

benedict-anderson.name: Benedict Anderson
benedict-anderson.summary: Anglo-Irish political scientist and historian (1936–2015), best known for his 1983 book Imagined Communities on the origins of nationalism; taught at Cornell.

imagined-communities.name: Imagined Communities
imagined-communities.summary: A 1983 book by Benedict Anderson that introduced the term 'imagined communities' to describe nations and became one of the most cited works in the social sciences.

cornell-paper.name: Cornell Paper
cornell-paper.summary: A January 1966 academic study by Benedict Anderson and Ruth McVey analyzing the failed 1965 coup attempt in Indonesia, arguing it was an internal army affair rather than a Communist-led plot.

30-september-movement.name: 30 September Movement
30-september-movement.summary: An alleged 1965 coup attempt in Indonesia blamed on the Communist Party, in which six army generals were assassinated; its suppression brought Suharto to power.

sangiran.name: Sangiran
sangiran.summary: An archaeological site in Java, Indonesia, ranked among the world's most important sites for studying fossil humans, alongside places like Zhoukoudian and Olduvai Gorge.

histoire-des-miao.name: Jean Michaud
histoire-des-miao.summary: Author of the Historical Dictionary of the Peoples of the Southeast Asian Massif, who wrote a critical study of Savina's 1924 ethnography of the Hmong people.

southeast-asian-massif.name: Southeast Asian Massif
southeast-asian-massif.summary: A term coined in 1997 for highland societies living above about 300 metres across parts of ten Southeast and South Asian countries, home to roughly 100 million indigenous people.

austronesian-peoples.name: Austronesian peoples
austronesian-peoples.summary: Peoples descended from a prehistoric seaborne migration out of Taiwan around 3000–1500 BCE, who used sails and outrigger boats to spread across the Indo-Pacific, from Madagascar to Easter Island and New Zealand.

austroasiatic-languages.name: Austroasiatic languages
austroasiatic-languages.summary: A family of about 168 languages spoken across Mainland Southeast Asia, South Asia and southern China, including Vietnamese and Khmer, the only two used as national languages.

b-o-i.name: Bảo Đại
b-o-i.summary: The 13th and final emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty (1913–1997), who ruled under French and later Japanese control before abdicating in 1945.

greater-east-asia-co-prosperity-sphere.name: Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere
greater-east-asia-co-prosperity-sphere.summary: A pan-Asian union Japan tried to build during World War II, covering Japan, Korea, Manchukuo, China and later parts of Southeast Asia, presented as economic cooperation but used as propaganda for Japanese dominance.

hachir-arita.name: Hachirō Arita
hachir-arita.summary: Japanese politician and diplomat who served as foreign minister three times and coined the term Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere used to justify Imperial Japan's expansion.

battle-of-dien-bien-phu.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
battle-of-dien-bien-phu.summary: The decisive 1954 battle in which Viet Minh forces under Võ Nguyên Giáp besieged and defeated French Union troops at Điện Biên Phủ, ending the First Indochina War.

viet-minh.name: Viet Minh
viet-minh.summary: A communist-led Vietnamese independence coalition founded by Ho Chi Minh in 1941, which proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after Japan's defeat in World War II.

state-of-vietnam.name: State of Vietnam
state-of-vietnam.summary: A Southeast Asian state existing from 1949 to 1955, first within the French Union and later fully independent, administering urban areas during the First Indochina War.

th-ch-qu-ng-c.name: Thích Quảng Đức
th-ch-qu-ng-c.summary: Vietnamese Mahayana Buddhist monk (c. 1897–1963) who set himself on fire in Saigon in 1963 to protest the South Vietnamese government's persecution of Buddhists.

ngo-dinh-diem.name: Ngo Dinh Diem
ngo-dinh-diem.summary: South Vietnamese politician who was the last prime minister of the State of Vietnam (1954-1955) and first president of South Vietnam (1955-1963), until his capture and assassination in a CIA-backed coup.

vichy-france.name: Vichy France
vichy-france.summary: The French state headed by Marshal Pétain from 1940 to 1944, formed after Germany's victory over France and based in the town of Vichy in the unoccupied 'free zone.'

battle-of-route-coloniale-4.name: Battle of Route Coloniale 4
battle-of-route-coloniale-4.summary: A 1950 battle of the First Indochina War along a French supply road near the Vietnam-China border, ending in a major French defeat after the Viet Minh received Chinese help.

james-c-scott.name: James C. Scott
james-c-scott.summary: An American political scientist and anthropologist (1936-2024) who studied peasant societies, state power and techniques non-state societies used to avoid state control.

the-art-of-not-being-governed.name: The Art of Not Being Governed
the-art-of-not-being-governed.summary: A 2009 book by anthropologist James C. Scott about Zomia, a highland Southeast Asian region whose many peoples have long avoided being ruled by surrounding states.
the-art-of-not-being-governed.source_title: The Art of Not Being Governed

sufism.name: Sufism
sufism.summary: An Islamic spiritual and ethical discipline concerned with purifying the self, closeness to God, and mystical experience, often described as Islamic mysticism.

abangan.name: Abangan
abangan.summary: Javanese Muslims who practice a syncretic form of Islam blending Hinduism, Buddhism and animism with local belief systems, unlike more orthodox Muslims.

pathet-lao.name: Pathet Lao
pathet-lao.summary: A communist political and military movement in Laos, backed by Vietnamese and Chinese communists, which took control of the country in 1975 after the civil war.

caodaism.name: Caodaism
caodaism.summary: A Vietnamese monotheistic religion founded in 1926 that blends Confucian ethics, Taoist practice, Buddhist ideas of karma and rebirth, and a Catholic-style hierarchy.

theosophy.name: Theosophy
theosophy.summary: A religious movement founded in the late 19th-century United States, drawing on Neoplatonism, Hinduism, and Buddhism, teaching spiritual emancipation through reincarnation and karma.

shirin-fozdar.name: Shirin Fozdar
shirin-fozdar.summary: Indian-born women's rights activist (1905–1992) who helped found the Singapore Council of Women and Syariah Court, and later opened a school in Thailand for girls at risk of forced prostitution.

bah-faith.name: Baháʼí Faith
bah-faith.summary: A religion founded by Baháʼu'lláh in 19th-century Iran teaching the unity of all religions and people, with 7 to 8 million followers worldwide today.

jade-emperor.name: Jade Emperor
jade-emperor.summary: A representation of the primordial god in Chinese mythology and folk religion, seen in Taoist theology as assistant to one of the Three Pure Ones.

queen-mother-of-the-west.name: Queen Mother of the West
queen-mother-of-the-west.summary: A mother goddess in Chinese religion and mythology, attested since Shang dynasty oracle-bone inscriptions and closely tied to Taoism; her cult, promising prosperity, longevity and bliss, grew especially under the Han dynasty.

nguy-n-b-nh-khi-m.name: Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm
nguy-n-b-nh-khi-m.summary: Vietnamese administrator, Confucianist, poet and prophet (1491–1585), later venerated as a saint of the Cao Dai religion and of the School of Teaching Goodness movement.

v-nh-b-o-district.name: Vĩnh Bảo District
v-nh-b-o-district.summary: A former rural district of Hải Phòng, Vietnam's third-largest city.

o-d-i.name: Áo dài
o-d-i.summary: A traditional Vietnamese outfit of a long split tunic worn over silk trousers, used as formalwear for both men and women.

chams.name: Cham people
chams.summary: An Austronesian people, the original inhabitants of coastal Vietnam and Cambodia, who founded the Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms of Champa from the 2nd century and became largely Muslim by the 17th century.

vietnamese-folk-religion.name: Thần
vietnamese-folk-religion.summary: In Vietnamese folk religion, thần refers broadly to spirits or gods, including nature deities, tutelary deities, and deified ancestral heroes.

new-order-indonesia.name: New Order (Indonesia)
new-order-indonesia.summary: The authoritarian regime of Indonesian President Suharto, from his rise to power in 1966 to his resignation in 1998, marked by military rule and repression of opponents.

hu.name: Huế
hu.summary: A city in central Vietnam that served as capital of Vietnam under the Nguyễn dynasty from 1802 to 1945, known today for its imperial palaces and tombs.

southeast_asia-modern-art-009: Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts
